Kastoria New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kastoria, Greece

Demolished. Kastoria's Jewish community, among the oldest in Greece, dates to the 6th century CE, later joined by Sephardi immigrants following the expulsions from Spain, Portugal, and Italy in the late 15th century. In the mid-17th century, Nathan of Gaza — chief theologian of the Sabbatean messianic movement — settled here and drew many of the community's leaders into that faith. By 1944, the entire Jewish quarter had been arrested and deported to the death camps; only a small community of 35 remained by 1945, and it declined further afterward. This newer of Kastoria's cemeteries, presumed established between the 18th and 19th centuries, has been completely destroyed, its site now covered by a military base, a nursing home, and an apartment block.
